_meta.reference_spec: cheapest plan with >=2 vCPU, >=4 GB RAM, >=40 GB SSD/NVMe, KVM-class virtualization
_meta.note: confidence=low means the price is a plausible market figure not confirmed against a live pricing page at compile time. The report must surface this.

providers.name: Hetzner Cloud
providers.abuse_style: Fast, manual abuse desk. Repeat complaints escalate to suspension quickly.
providers.notes: Best raw price/performance in the market. IPv4 billed separately (~EUR 0.50/mo). Abuse desk is the strictest of the budget EU hosts; Tor exits explicitly discouraged.

providers.name: netcup
providers.abuse_style: German host, standard notice-and-takedown. Reasonable but not permissive.
providers.notes: Exceptional RAM and disk per euro. No hourly billing and no real API; contract terms are rigid. Frequently cited as 2026 budget value leader.

providers.name: Contabo
providers.abuse_style: Tolerant in practice, slow support. Complaints handled by ticket, rarely instant suspension.
providers.notes: Unbeatable RAM per dollar and 11 locations. Well-documented CPU oversubscription and only a 200 Mbps port on entry tiers. No renewal price hike.

providers.name: OVHcloud
providers.abuse_style: Forwards complaints to customer with a response window. Famously hands-off unless ignored.
providers.notes: Truly unmetered egress is the standout feature for a browsing agent. Anti-DDoS included. IP ranges are widely blocklisted due to historical abuse.

providers.name: IONOS
providers.abuse_style: Corporate host with a compliance department. Conservative.
providers.notes: Strong SLA, but heavy KYC and a compliance-first posture. Introductory pricing rises sharply on renewal.

providers.name: Scaleway
providers.abuse_style: Strict; known for proactive suspension on abuse signals.
providers.notes: EU-only footprint kills the global-reach requirement. Good API and hourly billing.

providers.name: Time4VPS
providers.abuse_style: Baltic host, moderate. Forwards complaints.
providers.notes: Cheap on annual prepay but single-location, which fails the global-reach goal outright.

providers.name: Webdock
providers.abuse_style: Small, developer-friendly host with human support.
providers.notes: Clean IP reputation is its hidden advantage; small host, ranges not yet poisoned by abuse.

providers.name: LiteServer
providers.abuse_style: Dutch host, relaxed. Accepts crypto, minimal signup friction.
providers.notes: Permissive and cheap but single-location and no API.

providers.name: Zomro
providers.abuse_style: Markets itself as abuse-tolerant. Minimal verification.
providers.notes: Permissive, but shares ranges with abusive tenants which is exactly what poisons IP reputation for a browsing agent.

providers.name: Aeza Group
providers.abuse_style: Bulletproof-hosting reputation.
providers.notes: DISQUALIFIED. Sanctioned by the US Treasury (OFAC) in July 2025 as a bulletproof hosting provider. Transacting exposes you to sanctions liability, and payment rails will reject you.

providers.name: VDSina
providers.abuse_style: Relaxed, crypto-friendly.
providers.notes: Russian-jurisdiction billing entity creates payment and geopolitical risk for a long-lived production box.

providers.name: PQ.Hosting
providers.abuse_style: Permissive, crypto-friendly, minimal signup checks.
providers.notes: Best raw location count of any budget host (~40 sites). Independently verify the corporate structure and any sanctions exposure before committing.

providers.name: Gcore
providers.abuse_style: CDN operator with a real compliance function.
providers.notes: Outstanding global network reach, but priced as a CDN product and compliance-heavy.

providers.name: UpCloud
providers.abuse_style: Professional, proportionate.
providers.notes: A published 100% uptime SLA and the fastest storage in the class. Roughly 4x Hetzner's price for the same spec.

providers.name: Exoscale
providers.abuse_style: Swiss compliance posture, strict.
providers.notes: Swiss privacy jurisdiction, but EU-only and expensive.

providers.name: HOSTKEY
providers.abuse_style: Relaxed; Iceland location is notably tolerant.
providers.notes: Iceland footprint gives a genuinely permissive jurisdiction with EU-grade connectivity.

providers.name: DigitalOcean
providers.abuse_style: Automated fraud scoring locks accounts at signup, sometimes after payment. Well documented.
providers.notes: Excellent tooling and reliability. Aggressive automated KYC lockouts are a documented, recurring failure mode and directly contradict the permissiveness goal.

providers.name: Vultr
providers.abuse_style: Moderate. Accepts crypto, which lowers signup friction versus peers.
providers.notes: 32 locations is the best global coverage among reputable hosts, and it takes crypto. Price is 4-5x the budget tier.

providers.name: Akamai (Linode)
providers.abuse_style: Akamai-owned; enterprise compliance posture since acquisition.
providers.notes: 40 Gbps egress port is class-leading. Akamai ownership tightened the compliance posture considerably.

providers.name: AWS Lightsail
providers.abuse_style: AWS AUP enforcement. Scraping complaints escalate fast.
providers.notes: AWS ranges are the most aggressively blocked by anti-bot vendors of anything on this list. Worst possible choice for an agent that browses.

providers.name: Google Cloud (e2-medium)
providers.abuse_style: Strict AUP, automated abuse detection, project suspension.
providers.notes: Metered egress makes cost unpredictable for a browsing workload. Strictest AUP class on the list.

providers.name: Microsoft Azure (B2s)
providers.abuse_style: Enterprise compliance, strict.
providers.notes: Most locations of anything on this list, and the worst fit for the permissiveness goal.

providers.name: Oracle Cloud (Ampere A1)
providers.abuse_style: Free-tier accounts terminated with little recourse. Idle instances reclaimed.
providers.notes: Free tier halved to 2 OCPU / 12 GB as of 2026-06-15, with over-limit instances terminated from 2026-08-18. No SLA on free tier, capacity almost never available, and idle instances are reclaimed below 20% CPU. Free but not dependable for a 24/7 orchestrator.

providers.name: Alibaba Cloud
providers.abuse_style: Real-name verification, content compliance regime.
providers.notes: Heaviest KYC and content-compliance burden of anything here. Directly opposed to the stated goal.

providers.name: Tencent Cloud
providers.abuse_style: Same real-name/compliance regime as Alibaba.
providers.notes: Same structural problem as Alibaba for this use case.

providers.name: Civo
providers.abuse_style: Small cloud, human support.
providers.notes: Kubernetes-first; only 4 regions.

providers.name: Kamatera
providers.abuse_style: Notably hands-off for a mainstream provider. Fully configurable instances.
providers.notes: Rare combination: 24 global locations, hourly billing, permissive posture, and a real SLA. Priced mid-market.

providers.name: Hivelocity
providers.abuse_style: Bare-metal culture, hands-off.
providers.notes: 40 edge locations with a strong SLA and crypto accepted. Under-recognized for this use case.

providers.name: phoenixNAP
providers.abuse_style: Enterprise infrastructure provider.
providers.notes: 100% uptime SLA, enterprise-grade, priced accordingly.

providers.name: Latitude.sh
providers.abuse_style: Bare metal, hands-off.
providers.notes: Strong Latin America coverage that most providers lack. Far over budget for a single agent box.

providers.name: RackNerd
providers.abuse_style: Low-end market norms: forwards complaints, rarely proactive.
providers.notes: REPRICED 2026-08-09 from the live cart. Standing KVM-4GB is $24.59/mo (4 vCPU, 4 GB, 130 GB SSD RAID-10, 3 TB) and every plan shows an active Order Now button. The billing-cycle selector offers $24.59 monthly / $73.77 quarterly / $147.54 semi-annually / $295.08 annually — i.e. NO annual discount, so the earlier $3.62/mo (from a $43.39/year listing) was a time-limited promotional SKU that does not exist in the standing catalogue. RackNerd's cheap reputation rests entirely on those intermittent promos. Oversold nodes and no API.

providers.name: BuyVM (FranTech)
providers.abuse_style: Luxembourg location is explicitly DMCA-tolerant. Owner-operated, communicates directly with customers.
providers.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-08 against the live plan table. IMPORTANT: the widely-cited $15/mo SLICE 4096 is 4 GB with only ONE core, so it fails the 2-vCPU reference bar; the cheapest qualifying plan is the $30/mo High Volume 8 GB / 2 core. If one dedicated 3.5 GHz core is genuinely enough for Jod, the $15 slice is the single best permissiveness-per-dollar option on this list. Truly unmetered 1 Gbps, no overselling. Three locations only, and chronic out-of-stock.

providers.name: HostHatch
providers.abuse_style: Low-end market norms, relaxed.
providers.notes: REPRICED 2026-08-09 from the standing catalogue. The earlier $2.42/mo was a $29/year promotional SKU, not a price on the published product page. Standing list: NVMe 4 GB is $6/mo but ships only 20 GB of disk, and NVMe 8 GB ships 35 GB — both below the 40 GB reference spec. The cheapest plan that actually meets the spec is NVMe 12 GB at $12/mo (4 cores: 1 dedicated + 3 fair-shared, 12 GB, 50 GB NVMe, 3 TB). Compute VMs are in 7 locations; the APAC sites (Sydney, Hong Kong, Singapore) are storage VMs only, so the often-quoted 15-location figure overstates compute reach. Per-location stock is behind the panel login and was not confirmed. Support responsiveness is the recurring complaint.

providers.name: GreenCloudVPS
providers.abuse_style: Relaxed, crypto accepted.
providers.notes: Best Southeast Asia coverage in the budget tier, which matters if Jod needs low latency to APAC.

providers.name: Servarica
providers.abuse_style: Canadian jurisdiction, no DMCA regime as such. Relaxed.
providers.notes: CORRECTED 2026-08-09: every plan under $10/mo on the live listing reads 'Out of stock' — Shrimp 1 ($5/mo, 2 vCPU, 2 GB), Shrimp 2 ($7/mo) and Lobster ($10/mo, 4 vCPU, 3 GB). None of them is the 4 GB tier this row was priced at, and the cheap tiers are 'Unlimited Expanding Storage Offer' promos rather than standing catalogue entries. Unmetered bandwidth and a permissive Canadian jurisdiction remain genuine advantages, but effectively single-location and storage is spinning disk.

providers.name: Advin Servers
providers.abuse_style: Small US host, relaxed.
providers.notes: CORRECTED 2026-08-09 — this row was wrong twice over, and it was the previous recommendation. (1) There is no 4 GB / 2 vCPU plan in the catalogue; the $6.00 came from the homepage banner 'Starting at $6.00/month · 4GB RAM & 2 vCPU', which prices the $1.00/GB-of-memory rate rather than a buyable SKU. The smallest actual Standard plan is XS at 4 vCPU / 8 GB / 64 GB for $8/mo. (2) Every plan in the tier table reads 'Out of Stock' with a 'Get Notified' button, and all six regions report 'No Available Plans' — nothing is orderable at any size. The earlier city list (Dallas, Ashburn, Amsterdam, Singapore) was also wrong; the real six are Johor, Kansas City, Los Angeles, Miami, Nuremberg and NYC Metro. Memory-market shortages are the reported cause and the vendor has said it will not expand until DRAM pricing normalises.

providers.name: VirMach
providers.abuse_style: Very relaxed.
providers.notes: Extremely cheap, but a long documented history of extended outages, migrations, and support backlogs. Not suitable for a 24/7 orchestrator.

providers.name: InterServer
providers.abuse_style: US host, standard notice-and-takedown.
providers.notes: Price-lock guarantee is unusual and valuable for a long-lived box. US-only footprint.

providers.name: Hostwinds
providers.abuse_style: Standard US host.
providers.notes: Advertises a 99.999% SLA. Poor value at the reference spec and only 3 locations.

providers.name: VPSDime
providers.abuse_style: Relaxed low-end host.
providers.notes: CORRECTED 2026-08-09 against the live plan panel. The $7/mo plan is 4 vCPU / 6 GB / 30 GB SSD / 2 TB on a 10 Gbps port with an active 'Buy VPS Now ($7 USD)' button — not the 4 GB / 60 GB / 5 TB recorded earlier. 30 GB is below the 40 GB reference spec, so this row is correctly filtered out. A larger tier (the 12 GB tab) would clear the disk floor, but its price was not verified and is deliberately not guessed here. Strong RAM-per-dollar; only 3 locations and no API.

providers.name: Cloudzy
providers.abuse_style: Markets to VPN/RDP users; explicitly tolerant. Minimal signup friction.
providers.notes: 15 locations and a permissive posture, but its ranges are heavily used by VPN resellers, which harms IP reputation.

providers.name: Hostinger VPS
providers.abuse_style: Shared-hosting company culture: suspension-first on abuse signals.
providers.notes: Excellent headline price for 8 GB, but that requires a multi-year prepay and renewals jump sharply. Strictest AUP of the budget tier.

providers.name: ScalaHosting
providers.abuse_style: Managed-hosting culture, strict.
providers.notes: Managed-leaning; poor fit for an unmanaged agent box.

providers.name: UltaHost
providers.abuse_style: Moderate.
providers.notes: Aggressive introductory pricing with steep renewals.

providers.name: FlokiNET
providers.abuse_style: Explicitly free-speech oriented. Accepts Monero. Iceland/Romania jurisdictions chosen for legal resilience.
providers.notes: Among the most genuinely permissive hosts that is also legitimate and long-running. Expensive, EU-only, and no API.

providers.name: AbeloHost
providers.abuse_style: Bulgarian datacenter marketed as DMCA-ignored.
providers.notes: Long-established offshore host. Only 2 locations, both European.

providers.name: Shinjiru
providers.abuse_style: Long-running offshore specialist, explicitly DMCA-ignoring.
providers.notes: Maximum permissiveness with APAC presence. Expensive and bandwidth-capped.

providers.name: OrangeWebsite
providers.abuse_style: Icelandic free-speech hosting, anonymous signup accepted.
providers.notes: Single location in Iceland; fails global reach entirely.

providers.name: 1984 Hosting
providers.abuse_style: Privacy-first, but operates lawfully under Icelandic law rather than ignoring all process.
providers.notes: Genuinely privacy-respecting with very clean IP ranges, but only 2 European locations.

providers.name: Njalla
providers.abuse_style: Anonymity broker model: Njalla is the legal owner, you are the user.
providers.notes: Maximum anonymity, no SLA, minimal support, expensive. Optimized for a threat model Jod does not have.

providers.name: M247
providers.abuse_style: Carrier/network operator; supplies infrastructure to many VPN providers.
providers.notes: Exceptional global footprint (~40 sites) and VPN-friendly, but its ranges are consequently well known to anti-bot vendors.

providers.name: HostSlick
providers.abuse_style: Relaxed, crypto-friendly, offshore-leaning.
providers.notes: Unmetered bandwidth at a low price with a permissive posture. Only 3 locations.

providers.name: IncogNET
providers.abuse_style: Privacy-first, anonymous signup, Monero accepted. Luxembourg location DMCA-tolerant.
providers.notes: REPRICED 2026-08-09 from the live plan grid. The earlier $12.00 was the 2 GB plan (1 vCPU, 30 GB), which does not meet the reference spec — copying a cheaper tier's price onto a larger tier's specs is exactly the error this correction pass exists to remove. The real 4 GB plan is $20/mo: 2 vCPU, 50 GB NVMe, 10 TB, 2.5 Gbps. Stock is partial and the vendor publishes it per plan per location: at the 4 GB tier Liberty Lake, Stockholm and Sofia are orderable while Valley Forge, Kansas City and Amsterdam are sold out, and every tier at 10 GB and above is out of stock everywhere. Six VPS POPs, not the ~10 POPs the network page advertises (the rest are VPN/DNS only). No PII required, Monero accepted, independently listed as no-KYC. Operating since 2020.

providers.name: PRQ
providers.abuse_style: Legendary for refusing takedowns. Effectively no support.
providers.notes: Maximum legal resilience, minimal service. Single location, no SLA, no API.

providers.name: Melbicom
providers.abuse_style: Network operator, hands-off.
providers.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-08: 21 datacenters, KVM, NVMe. CORRECTION: 'unmetered' is qualified — 1 Gbps is throttled to 100 Mbit/s past a 5 TB monthly quota, Fujairah and Mumbai are hard-capped at 2-5 TB, and users report Asian links as slow as 10 Mbps. Scored as 5 TB metered, not unmetered. Reviews report 300+ day uptime streaks and responsive support.

providers.name: VPSServer.com
providers.abuse_style: Moderate.
providers.notes: Broad location list with hourly billing. Mid-market pricing.

providers.name: OVH Kimsufi / SoYouStart
providers.abuse_style: Same hands-off OVH abuse process.
providers.notes: Dedicated hardware with no CPU steal and unmetered egress, at VPS money. Older hardware and slow provisioning.

providers.name: Fly.io
providers.abuse_style: Strict; aggressive anti-abuse after crypto-mining waves.
providers.notes: EXCLUDED: Firecracker microVMs behind a managed PaaS. No persistent root box semantics, metered egress, strict AUP, and dedicated IPv4 costs extra.

providers.name: Railway
providers.abuse_style: Very strict; bans scraping and automation workloads outright in practice.
providers.notes: EXCLUDED: managed container PaaS, no root VM, strictest AUP class, metered egress.
